evidence.text: Power indication: lit. The call panel reports power at the lift. Power indication does not prove a data link. Source: lift call panel; observed in The Arrival Lift.

Link indication: unlit. The separate link lamp reports no indicated link. The lamp is not a diagnosis of the cause. End-to-end service is not proven. Source: link indicator beside the arrival tube; observed in The Arrival Lift.

Physical inspection. Trace Lift Sender A through the selected conduit and the 10 m workshop patch lead to Workshop Receiver B. The service-loop conduit is 95 m (105 m total); the direct conduit is 85 m (95 m total). These are the supplied T02/T01 lengths in the fictional PROFILE-COPPER-100, whose inclusive limit is 100 m. Record the selected path and measured result at the current configuration and attempt. Valid inspection recorded means the inspection was performed, even when length exceeds the profile. It does not mean the link or a service works. A changed path leaves the old result stale until a new inspection. Source: labeled training conduit and inspection kit in The Arrival Lift; PHY04; T01/T02.

alternatives.label: Record both indications and validate the inspection
alternatives.explanation: Both indicators must have been observed separately and a valid current inspection performed. A correctly recorded over-limit result is valid inspection evidence; do not demand a passing length result or mark the link repaired.

method.text: Start with observations: which indicator reports power and which reports the link?

workedStep.text: Look at POWER and LINK separately. Take the inspection kit from the satchel, then inspect the labeled path.

solution.text: Record the lit power indication and the unlit link indication, then Use Inspect physical path with the reusable kit. Keep the measured result even if it exceeds the fictional limit.

records.observableOutcome: The notebook holds separate power and link observations plus a sourced current physical inspection. O01 is Completed.
records.completionExplanation: You distinguished two indications and inspected the actual declared path. End-to-end service is not proven. The result is evidence to carry to the workshop, not a repaired network.

evidence.text: Known-good endpoints: Lift Sender A — known good; Workshop Receiver B — known good. Each passed the supplied local bench check before this exercise. Their known-good status is a declared scenario premise, not proof that the connecting path or an end-to-end service works. Source: signed bench cards on the topology relief table in The Titan's Workshop; PHY02 / C-SCOPE.
Lift Sender A — known good. Near endpoint: the labeled sender behind the lift call panel. Bench card A declares the local sender functional for this fictional exercise.
Workshop Receiver B — known good. Far endpoint: the receiver in the workshop dispatch console. Bench card B declares the local receiver functional for this fictional exercise.

Physical path under test, in order: Lift Sender A → selected training conduit → workshop patch lead → Workshop Receiver B. Initial conduit: service loop, 95 m; alternative direct conduit: 85 m. The patch lead is 10 m in either configuration. The fixture declares compatible endpoints, media and terminations; the inspection grades length only. This path is the declared-path role of C-SCOPE, not the whole Iron City network. Source: topology relief table and matching conduit labels, The Titan's Workshop.

Investigation scope. Inspect the physical path between known-good endpoints. Pin a testable hypothesis, keep it separate from observed evidence, and decide what observation would support or challenge it. Physical transmission represents bits; it does not select an IP route or verify an application login. Source: the Titan in The Titan's Workshop; PHY02 / S01, S02, S04.

solution.text: Identify Lift Sender A and Workshop Receiver B, identify their declared physical path, and pin your own testable hypothesis. Its diagnosis need not agree with the author.
